checks.result: passed; negotiated MCP 2025-06-18 and advertised tools/resources
passed; initialize, tools/list, and actionable app_unavailable tool result

acceptance_evidence.reference: The new disk-witness-mcp executable implements MCP initialization, initialized notification, ping, stable tools/resources discovery, resource reads, calls, cancellation state, JSON-RPC protocol errors, and actionable tool execution errors. It exposes exactly seven closed and bounded read-only tools, defensively strips content/environment/credential fields and redacts secret-like arguments, and rejects oversized results. The connector never opens SQLite; its Unix-domain client requires a current-user socket with no group/other permissions. The menu-bar app now owns a 0600 socket, verifies peer UID and PID, and serves live summary, explanations, provenance, registered process contexts, inferred task impact, review-only cleanup candidates, and an inline bundle produced by the same EvidenceBundleExporter. Real socket tests register/end a session, insert retained evidence, query it, verify task impact, and compare inline export structure.

discovered_risks: macOS Unix-domain socket paths are length-limited; the product Application Support path is checked at startup and reports degraded IPC if it cannot bind.

MCP cancellation is checked before and during IPC reads/writes; the current line-oriented runner processes one request at a time, so a later cancellation notification cannot preempt a server call already blocking in that same stdio process.
Registered process contexts are reported as tool-linked and are not labeled proven writers; exact attribution remains unavailable until the optional privileged observer is installed.
Inline evidence export uses temporary app-owned bundle files and removes each completed bundle after encoding the response.
